original_question: In Theorem 29, a multiplicative subgroup R = v·U modulo a prime p is required to have size at least 10^8 p^(7/8) log^(5/2) p in order to guarantee an element a in R with bounded continued-fraction sum and hence discrepancy D(a,p) << log p log log p. Can the exponent 7/8 in that size condition be replaced by a smaller exponent?
target_in_paper: The sharpening problem attached to Theorem 29 in the paper’s Zaremba/good-lattice-point section: lowering the exponent 7/8 in the subgroup-coset size hypothesis for R=vU\subset (\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times while keeping the same continued-fraction/discrepancy conclusion.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the exact theorem number, the ambient mod-p multiplicative-coset setting R=v\cdot U, the precise threshold 10^8 p^{7/8}(\log p)^{5/2}, and the intended conclusion: existence of an element a\in R whose continued-fraction data are small enough to yield the discrepancy bound D(a,p)\ll \log p\,\log\log p. It also asks for the right local strengthening: whether the exponent 7/8 can be reduced, rather than broadening to the full Zaremba conjecture or to arbitrary subsets.
missing_details: State explicitly that p is a prime and U is a multiplicative subgroup of (\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times, with v\in (\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times and R=vU a coset.
Specify that the continued fraction is the finite continued-fraction expansion of the rational number a/p, and that the bounded quantity is the sum of its partial quotients.

Make the quantifiers explicit: ask whether there exists an absolute exponent \beta<7/8 (and corresponding absolute constants) such that the theorem remains true uniformly for every prime p, every subgroup U, and every coset R=vU satisfying the new size condition.

If discrepancy is mentioned, define D(a,p) as the discrepancy of the Korobov/Larcher lattice-point set associated with a modulo p; in the paper the continued-fraction bound is the primary conclusion and the discrepancy bound is deduced from the preceding result.

Clarify whether the logarithmic factor (\log p)^{5/2} is intended to remain exactly as in Theorem 29, or whether only the power of p is being questioned; to stay closest to the paper, the question should only target the exponent of p.
State that the implied constants in \ll are absolute, as in the theorem’s style.
refined_question: Let p be a prime, let U\subset (\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times be a multiplicative subgroup, let v\in (\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times, and put R=vU. Theorem 29 in arXiv:1202.4539 asserts that if |R|\ge 10^8 p^{7/8}(\log p)^{5/2}, then there exists a\in R such that, writing a/p=[b_1,\dots,b_\ell] for the finite continued-fraction expansion of a/p, one has \sum_{j=1}^\ell b_j\ll \log p\,\log\log p (and hence, by the preceding discrepancy estimate used in the paper, D(a,p)\ll \log p\,\log\log p). Can the exponent 7/8 in this size hypothesis be replaced by some smaller absolute exponent \beta<7/8, uniformly in p, U, and v, while keeping the same conclusion?
justification: The draft is already tightly aimed at the paper’s actual later-section theorem rather than at a broader neighboring problem. What it lacked was only the full stand-alone formulation: the precise ambient group, the fact that R is a coset rather than an arbitrary subset, the exact object whose continued-fraction sum is bounded, and the uniform quantifiers over p, U, and v. The paper’s intent here is a very specific quantitative improvement problem attached to Theorem 29, not a reformulation of Zaremba’s full conjecture. Because the discrepancy statement is presented as a consequence of the continued-fraction bound via the preceding result, the refined question keeps the continued-fraction conclusion primary and asks only for a smaller exponent in the theorem’s hypothesis.
